meta.title: BSO - The Missing Social Layer of Crypto
meta.description: BSO is the money of Bitsocial, the peer-to-peer social network that no company owns. An Ethereum L2 appchain where communities own their networks, their tokens and their revenue.

hero.statusCta: Chain is not live yet, subscribe for updates
hero.title: The missing <mark>social layer</mark> of crypto
hero.supporting: Crypto became a casino because Web2, TradFi, and centralized infrastructure own the distribution rails and bend the incentives. Bitsocial Chain fixes this: an unstoppable, fully decentralized <l2Link>Ethereum L2</l2Link> <appchainLink>appchain</appchainLink> where communities own their networks, their tokens and their revenue.

layers.ariaLabel: Three stacked layers of crypto: social apps on the Bitsocial network on top, Ethereum L1 settlement at the base, and Bitsocial Chain, the Ethereum L2 appchain powered by BSO, igniting as the glowing missing layer that slots into the gap between them, threaded by an energy spine.

whyAChain.title: Bitsocial itself is not on a blockchain.
whyAChain.supporting: Posts, profiles, communities and moderation on <bitsocialLink>Bitsocial</bitsocialLink> are peer-to-peer. No chain, no fees, no wallet: you can use the whole network without ever touching crypto, and most people will. But a few things genuinely need a chain — names that are yours, money that moves between strangers, tokens a community actually owns. Bitsocial Chain is for exactly those, and nothing else.

peerToPeer.note: The social network. No chain involved.

onChain.note: The few parts that need one.

whyAChain.caption: The chain is optional. The social network is not.
whyAChain.quote: A decentralized social network needs decentralized money.

tokenomics.title: Sound money.
tokenomics.supporting: BSO is a fixed-supply ERC-20: 210 million, no inflation, deflationary by design. It was given away in 2022 through three airdrops and liquidity-mining rewards, with no presale and no team allocation. Its contract is immutable and adminless, so the rules are fixed forever.

airdrop.label: The distribution
airdrop.note: Three airdrop rounds in January and February 2022, claimed by 1,510 addresses. Round 1 used a Telegram bot with referral bonuses, and Esteban reviewed its referrals by hand for abuse; rounds 2 and 3 ran on Twitter and Reddit. About 63% of all PLEB went out through the airdrops and 34% as rewards to people who provided liquidity; the rest seeded the launch pools. No presale, no team allocation, nothing sold.
airdrop.richListLink: See every holder and all three rounds

contract.label: The whole contract
contract.note: The full supply mints to one address because that is how the migration works: balances were mirrored one-for-one onto it and paid back out by transfer, every one of them on-chain. Everything else is <openZeppelinLink>OpenZeppelin</openZeppelinLink>, unmodified — the most used and most reviewed token code in Ethereum. Nothing custom, nothing clever. Read it on <etherscanLink>Etherscan</etherscanLink>.

tokenomics.foot: Immutable and adminless: there are no admin keys left to hold, so nobody can change it, inflate it, or freeze it.

unstoppable.title: Built on Ethereum. Run by nobody.
unstoppable.supporting: A new blockchain would rebuild the security and developer base Ethereum already has, and would need a new token when BSO is already fully distributed. So Bitsocial Chain is designed as an Ethereum L2 with no operator: every action is a plain Ethereum transaction sent to an address nobody controls, and anyone can run a node that derives the same state from Ethereum's history. There is no company to pressure and no switch to flip.

noAdminKeys.label: No admin keys
noAdminKeys.note: nobody changes the rules for you

noPrivilegedNode.label: No privileged node
noPrivilegedNode.note: anyone can derive the same state

unstoppable.proofOfConcept: The proof of concept already derives .bso names this way, on a local dev chain. A production launch still needs a proof system, an audit and final economics. <proofLink>Read the proof of concept</proofLink>.

bsoNames.title: Your .bso name stays yours.
bsoNames.supporting: Bitsocial apps <resolverLink>resolve .bso names today</resolverLink> by borrowing ENS, the naming system Ethereum wallets use: mycommunity.bso is really mycommunity.eth carrying a bitsocial record. A native registry would airdrop every name already in use to the wallet that holds it — nothing to claim and nothing to re-register.

communityMoney.title: One asset under many communities.
communityMoney.supporting: Each community could run its own layer, an L3 with its own token, and pay its fees, names and rent in BSO. L3s already exist across crypto; on Bitsocial Chain one would arrive with a community already attached. Its revenue could settle itself: ad slots auctioned by contract, part of every sale destroyed on the spot and the rest paid to the community, with no buyback treasury for anyone to capture.
communityMoney.feesFlow: fees, names and rent paid in BSO
communityMoney.chainMeta: Ethereum layer · its state derives from Ethereum
communityMoney.caption: A share of every fee is destroyed; the rest pays for the chain's security.

privacy.title: Tipping shouldn't dox you.
privacy.supporting: Bitsocial Chain is public by default, like Ethereum, and .bso names are meant to be seen. Money is different: a tip should never require putting your name, profile or post on-chain beside it, and a fresh wallet should be normal, not suspicious. The chain won't build its own privacy system. It is meant to let existing ones plug in without asking permission: shielded pools, stealth addresses, zero-knowledge proofs.

possibilities.title: Proposed, in the open.
possibilities.supporting: Not live yet. BSO is live on Ethereum today; Bitsocial Chain is a proposal, and its first proof of concept, native .bso names, runs on a local dev chain. Nothing below has a date. It is what a social layer with its own money would make possible: some of it will get built, some replaced by better ideas, and some built by people who have not shown up yet.

verify.title: Only one address is BSO.
verify.supporting: Anyone can create a token and call it BSO, so the contract address is the only thing that tells the real one apart. Match all 42 characters against this site and Bitsocial's official channels before sending anything anywhere.
verify.warning: The official BSO contract is <contract>{{address}}</contract>. Anything else is not BSO, whatever it is called and wherever it is listed.
verify.note: Liquidity on Uniswap is provided by independent people, and anyone can add to it. It is not a savings account: the value of a liquidity position can fall, including below what was put in.

linked.title: Linked wallets
linked.lead: Wallets are grouped only when the chain shows a link: tokens or gas moving between them, a shared private funder, a multisig owner, or an identical buying pattern. Each group lists the transactions behind it.

confidence.confirmed: The wallets transact with each other, share a private funder, or control one another.
confidence.likely: Several transfers from one source that are hard to explain any other way.
confidence.possible: A single link that could also be a sale or a gift.

holderA.name: Holder A
holderA.summary: Twelve wallets that bought PLEB on Avalanche between February 22 and April 8, 2022, and have never sold. Five are tied together on-chain; the other seven match the same buyer's pattern.

evidence.transfersToLpWallet: Two of the buying wallets sent PLEB and AVAX to a third wallet, which used them for Trader Joe liquidity and farming: 1B PLEB and 5 AVAX on February 27, 2022, then 7.2B PLEB and 34 AVAX between February 28 and March 2. The third wallet sent 0.013 AVAX back.
evidence.sharedFunder: One private wallet funded three of the buying wallets and nothing else. Every transaction it ever sent went to them, in order: nonces 0 to 4 to the first, 5 to 7 to the second, 8 to the third.
evidence.buyingPattern: Seven more wallets were each new, funded by one or two exchange withdrawals of about $2,000 to $3,400 through Binance or ChangeNOW (the same services the linked wallets used), swapped entirely into PLEB and never used again. They bought one after another between February 28 and March 31, 2022, never overlapping with the linked wallets. Of all 292 PLEB buyers from February to April 2022, no other wallet fits this pattern.
evidence.neverSold: None of the twelve wallets has sold or moved its tokens since. Their balances came through both migrations unchanged.

holderB.name: Holder B
holderB.summary: A 2-of-4 Safe multisig that gathered PLEB from 14 wallets in one afternoon, plus one of its owners.

evidence.owners: The Safe needs 2 of its 4 owners to sign. One owner also holds BSO directly. Four owners can mean one person with several keys or a small group.
evidence.consolidation: On June 1, 2024, between 16:08 and 17:51 UTC, the Safe received 120.5B PLEB from 14 wallets. The first transfer was a 10-token test that the Safe sent straight back.
evidence.vesting: On August 12, 2024, the Safe moved 60.5B PLEB into a Sablier vesting stream. The 2026 migration credited that stream back to the Safe, which is why the Safe received two migration transfers.
evidence.commonSender: The same wallet sent PLEB to both the Safe owner (13.7B on March 8, 2024) and the Safe (1.5B on June 1, 2024).

holderC.name: Holder C
holderC.summary: Two wallets that received PLEB from the same sender.

evidence.commonSender: One wallet sent 4.7B PLEB to the first on August 19, 2024 and 15.4B to the second on November 14, 2025. A shared sender can also be one seller serving two buyers.

holderD.name: Holder D
holderD.summary: Three wallets joined through one of them.

evidence.sharedRecipient: The middle wallet received a test transfer and then 5B PLEB from the first on November 18, 2022, and 8.2B PLEB from the third on December 1, 2022. It could also be one buyer paying two sellers.

holderE.name: Holder E
holderE.summary: Two wallets filled from the same source.

evidence.commonSender: One wallet sent the first 39.4B PLEB in seven transfers between October 2024 and January 2025, and the second 2.0B on November 22, 2025.

holderF.name: Holder F
holderF.summary: One wallet that split its tokens into three new wallets and paid their gas.

evidence.split: On March 10, 2024, within seven minutes, one wallet sent round amounts of PLEB (12B, 8B and 4B) to three new wallets and sent two of them ETH for gas the same day. It still holds BSO itself.

holderG.name: Holder G
holderG.summary: Two wallets funded by the same sender, three years apart.

evidence.commonSender: One wallet sent the second 4.7B PLEB on Avalanche in April 2022 and the first 6B PLEB on Ethereum in January 2025.

holderH.name: Holder H
holderH.summary: Two wallets with one transfer between them.

evidence.directTransfer: The first wallet sent the second 420M PLEB on April 24, 2022.

holderI.name: Holder I
holderI.summary: Two wallets with repeated transfers between them.

evidence.directTransfers: The second wallet sent the first 13.2B PLEB on October 30, 2023 and 5B on November 8, 2023.

facts.liquiditySeed: The only mint to a team wallet outside the airdrop was the launch liquidity: 50B PLEB, added to the Trader Joe pool (40.1B) and the Pangolin pool (10B) within seven minutes on January 14, 2022.
facts.teamClaims: Two team members claimed in round 1: Esteban 5B PLEB, and Tom 13.2B PLEB, the third-largest of 767 claims. Together that is 2% of all PLEB claimed in the airdrops.
facts.noFarmRewards: No team wallet received liquidity-mining rewards. The 433B paid out on Avalanche went to 208 other addresses, and the 57B still unpaid at the move to Ethereum was credited to the stakers who had earned it.
facts.migrationMintedNothing: The 2026 migration created no new tokens for anyone: all 210M BSO went out in one transaction, in proportion to old balances.

history.title: History
history.lead: From a Telegram group in 2021 to an immutable ERC-20 in 2026.

groupOpens.title: The plebbit Telegram group opens
groupOpens.body: The group that is now t.me/bitsocialnet starts on Christmas Day 2021.

telegramRound.title: Round 1: the Telegram bot
telegramRound.body: For a week, people sign up with @plebbitbot. The supply is split equally among participants, with bonuses for referrals. 3,312 addresses register before the bot closes on January 14.

launch.title: Liquidity first, then claims
launch.body: At 18:00 UTC the deployer adds PLEB and 7 AVAX to Trader Joe and Pangolin. The claim page opens about 30 minutes later, so every allocation was fixed before anyone could trade.

twitterRound.title: Round 2: Twitter
twitterRound.body: An airdrop run entirely on Twitter: like, retweet and tag three friends. Over 1,500 people register by February 6.

redditRound.title: Round 3: Reddit
redditRound.body: An experimental airdrop on r/plebbitairdrop, where a bot checked that commenters had older Reddit activity. Over 2,200 register by February 12, many of them bots.

claimsClose.title: Claims close
claimsClose.body: All three airdrops become unclaimable. Tokens nobody claimed are never minted.

farm.title: Liquidity mining starts
farm.body: People who stake PLEB/AVAX liquidity earn newly minted PLEB. The farm pays out until the move to Ethereum.

ethereum.title: The move to Ethereum
ethereum.body: After a Snapshot vote, PLEB is frozen and every balance, including locked tokens, liquidity positions and unpaid farm rewards, is re-issued on Ethereum as the second-generation token. Holders do nothing.

rebrand.title: plebbit becomes Bitsocial
rebrand.body: plebbit announces its new name, Bitsocial. On-chain, the token keeps the PLEB name until May.

rebase.title: PLEB becomes 210 million BSO
rebase.body: The second-generation token is renamed BSO and rebased so the total supply is exactly 210 million: 7,114.6 PLEB become 1 BSO.

immutable.title: BSO becomes immutable
immutable.body: The final BSO contract goes live with no mint, owner, pause or proxy. All 210M go out in one transaction, in proportion to the rebased balances.

method.title: Method and limits
method.lead: How the groups were found, and what this page cannot see.

how.transfers: Every transfer of PLEB and BSO between two ordinary wallets, on Avalanche and Ethereum, was traced, leaving out exchanges, routers, pools and other contracts. Safe multisigs were linked to their owners.
how.funders: The first wallet to send each top holder AVAX or ETH was compared. Exchanges fund thousands of wallets, so only private funders count as a link.
how.pattern: For wallets with no direct link, buying behavior was compared against every PLEB buyer of the same period.
how.migrations: Balances were followed through both migrations at 7,114.6 PLEB per BSO.

limits.exchangeOnly: A holder who funds every wallet through an exchange and never moves tokens between them leaves no on-chain link. Some groups may still hide more wallets.
limits.sales: A transfer between two wallets can be a sale or a gift. Groups marked Possible rest on a single link like that.
limits.contracts: Tokens held by contracts other than the Uniswap pool and the Safe are listed as they are.
limits.snapshot: Balances and the price refresh from the chain every five minutes while this page is open. The links between wallets are researched by hand and do not update on their own.
limits.history: History lines follow what each wallet held, for wallets with at least 0.01% of the supply and every wallet of a known holder. Tokens in a liquidity pool, farm or vesting stream leave the line, and the migrations re-issued some of them to their owners, so some lines jump on those days.

method.title: How the chart is built
method.lead: Every candle comes from swaps on the chain, so any day can be checked on an explorer.

steps.swaps: A day's open, high, low and close are the first, highest, lowest and last price paid in that day's swaps, in UTC, read from each pool's Swap events.
steps.usd: Pools trade against AVAX or ETH, so each swap is converted to dollars at Coinbase's rate for the hour it happened.
steps.units: PLEB, on Avalanche and on Ethereum until the <rebaseLink>rebase on May 2, 2026</rebaseLink>, is shown per BSO: its price is multiplied by 7,114.596, the number of PLEB each BSO replaced.
steps.pools: When more than one pool traded on a day, the one with the most volume sets that day's candle, so a nearly empty pool cannot draw a false wick. Volume adds up every pool, and a day without trades repeats the last close.
steps.mcap: Market cap is the close times that day's total supply: every token the contract minted minus every token it burned, converted to BSO like the price. After the rebase, and for BSO today, the supply is the fixed 210 million.
steps.eras: Each contract's history ends at the first trade of the next one. The Ethereum contract kept the PLEB name until the upgrade that rebased it, six weeks after plebbit became Bitsocial on March 18, 2026.

protocolLabsGrant.title: A grant from Protocol Labs
protocolLabsGrant.body: Protocol Labs, the team behind IPFS and Filecoin, gives plebbit a grant to build its decentralized Reddit alternative.

firstApp.title: The first plebbit app
firstApp.body: The first desktop app ships for Linux, Windows and Mac. It runs its own IPFS node, so unlike the web demo it is fully peer-to-peer.

plebchan.title: plebchan launches
plebchan.body: plebchan, a 4chan-style app on the plebbit protocol, publishes its first release, for the web, Mac and Linux.

hackerNews.title: Front page of Hacker News
hackerNews.body: Amid the backlash over Reddit's new API pricing, the plebbit demo reaches the Hacker News front page with over 300 points. The same week, posts about it reach the front page of r/ethereum and draw 30,000 views on r/CryptoCurrency.

coingecko.title: Listed on CoinGecko
coingecko.body: After turning it down several times since early 2022, CoinGecko lists PLEB.

socialFi.title: In CoinGecko's SocialFi category
socialFi.body: CoinGecko adds PLEB to its SocialFi category after the team asks, and a list of SocialFi tokens shared on X includes it. The price nearly doubles in five days.

seedit.title: Seedit launches
seedit.body: Seedit, an app that looks and works like old Reddit, publishes its first release.

marchRally.title: The March 2024 rally
marchRally.body: On March 1, investor Jason Calacanis tweets that he wants a distributed, permissionless Reddit, and plebbit replies with its demo. Seedit 0.1.6 ships on March 3, and on March 4 the team announces token-gated communities. With ETH passing $4,000 that month, the price nearly doubles on March 4 and triples by the end of March, on $2.2 million of volume, the most of any month on this chart.
